title: Maintain Product Inspection Standards
description: Continue routine checks so current product quality remains consistent as orders and suppliers change.
actions: Keep a regular sample-inspection schedule.
Record defects and returns by product batch.
Review supplier quality periodically.
reasoning: Current feedback indicates little quality-related concern, so preventive controls are appropriate.

title: Preserve Consistent Product Performance
description: Protect the dependable product experience by checking that items continue to match expected specifications.
actions: Use a consistent checklist for incoming stock.
Compare product samples against approved specifications.
Document any change in materials or manufacturing.
reasoning: Ongoing specification checks help detect small variations before they affect customers.

title: Keep Product Information Accurate
description: Ensure product pages set realistic expectations and remain aligned with the items customers receive.
actions: Review descriptions and specifications after product changes.
Use clear photos that represent the actual item.
Correct outdated compatibility or sizing details.
reasoning: Accurate information supports customer expectations and helps prevent avoidable quality complaints.

title: Continue Preventive Quality Reviews
description: Use routine feedback reviews to maintain quality and identify emerging patterns early.
actions: Review recent reviews and return reasons on a schedule.
Track recurring product terms in feedback.
Assign an owner to investigate any new pattern.
reasoning: A lightweight review process can catch emerging concerns without unnecessary disruption.

title: Sustain Supplier Quality Controls
description: Maintain a reliable supply process through regular supplier communication and documented acceptance criteria.
actions: Keep written acceptance criteria for incoming goods.
Share recurring feedback themes with suppliers.
Reassess suppliers when quality patterns change.
reasoning: Consistent supplier controls help preserve current performance over time.

title: Strengthen Product Consistency Checks
description: Make product quality checks more consistent across batches, variants, and suppliers.
actions: Compare samples from different batches.
Record defects using a common category list.
Review variations before restocking.
reasoning: Minor quality-related signals may benefit from tighter consistency checks.

title: Review Product Feedback Trends
description: Look for small recurring concerns that could become more significant if left unaddressed.
actions: Group feedback by product and defect type.
Check whether concerns cluster around a variant or batch.
Prioritise repeatable patterns over isolated comments.
reasoning: Trend analysis helps distinguish one-off experiences from a developing quality issue.

title: Refresh Product Specifications
description: Confirm that specifications and product descriptions match the current item and customer use cases.
actions: Verify dimensions, materials, compatibility, and included parts.
Update unclear or outdated statements.
Ask support staff to flag expectation mismatches.
reasoning: Small gaps between description and delivered product can create preventable dissatisfaction.

title: Improve Incoming Stock Checks
description: Add targeted checks for product attributes that customers mention most often.
actions: Inspect the attributes most frequently discussed in reviews.
Sample stock from newly received batches.
Escalate repeated failures to the supplier.
reasoning: Targeted checks provide an efficient way to investigate modest quality concerns.

title: Close the Feedback Loop with Suppliers
description: Share specific, evidence-based feedback with suppliers to prevent repeat issues.
actions: Provide examples and batch details where available.
Agree on corrective actions and review dates.
Verify changes in later deliveries.
reasoning: Supplier follow-up can reduce recurring variation and improve consistency.

title: Improve Product Quality and Customer Expectations
description: Review recurring quality concerns and make product performance and descriptions more consistent.
actions: Analyse negative feedback by product and issue.
Improve materials, components, or quality checks where evidence supports it.
Make product descriptions and limitations explicit.
reasoning: Repeated quality-related feedback suggests that focused investigation and improvement are warranted.

title: Investigate Recurring Product Defects
description: Identify whether reported defects share a product, batch, supplier, or usage pattern before choosing corrective action.
actions: Create a defect log with dates and product identifiers.
Inspect relevant samples and returned items.
Agree on corrective actions with the responsible supplier or team.
reasoning: A structured investigation reduces the risk of treating symptoms while the underlying issue continues.

title: Align Product Claims with Actual Performance
description: Reduce expectation gaps by ensuring marketing claims and specifications reflect observed product performance.
actions: Audit claims against verified product specifications.
Clarify limitations and compatibility requirements.
Update customer-facing content where needed.
reasoning: Expectation mismatches can contribute to negative reviews even when the item is functioning as designed.

title: Strengthen Quality Assurance Before Dispatch
description: Introduce a focused pre-dispatch check for products linked to repeated customer concerns.
actions: Define checks for the affected product categories.
Record pass/fail outcomes for sampled orders.
Review results and adjust checks based on evidence.
reasoning: Additional targeted checks can prevent avoidable defects from reaching customers.

title: Prioritise the Most Frequent Quality Issues
description: Use review and return data to focus improvement work on the quality issues affecting customers most often.
actions: Rank issues by frequency and customer impact.
Assign owners and target dates for the top issues.
Measure whether complaints decline after changes.
reasoning: Prioritisation helps direct effort toward recurring issues rather than isolated anecdotes.

title: Resolve Major Product Quality Issues
description: Investigate repeated reports of defects or poor performance and take proportionate corrective action for affected products.
actions: Inspect relevant inventory and returned items promptly.
Pause sale or dispatch of a batch only when evidence indicates a material defect or safety concern.
Work with suppliers on a documented corrective plan.
reasoning: Frequent or serious quality complaints may indicate a material problem that needs prompt investigation.

title: Contain and Correct Confirmed Defects
description: Prevent further customer impact when a specific product or batch is confirmed to have a significant defect.
actions: Identify affected SKUs, batches, and orders.
Quarantine affected stock when justified by inspection findings.
Arrange repair, replacement, refund, or supplier remediation as appropriate.
reasoning: Containment is appropriate when evidence confirms a significant defect; avoid broad restrictions without product-level evidence.

title: Launch a Quality Root-Cause Review
description: Coordinate a focused review to determine why substantial quality complaints are recurring.
actions: Bring together operations, support, and supplier contacts.
Compare complaints with inspection and return records.
Document root cause, corrective actions, owners, and verification steps.
reasoning: A root-cause review helps prevent repeated failures and supports accountable corrective action.

title: Improve Quality Verification for Affected Products
description: Increase verification for products associated with repeated negative quality feedback until performance is stable.
actions: Define measurable acceptance criteria.
Inspect incoming batches more frequently for the affected items.
Return to normal checks only after results support the change.
reasoning: Temporary, targeted verification can reduce recurrence while avoiding unnecessary disruption to unaffected products.

title: Contact Affected Customers with a Resolution Plan
description: Provide clear, fair support to customers who report a verified product problem.
actions: Confirm the issue and gather relevant order details.
Explain available replacement, repair, or refund options.
Track cases through resolution and review repeat complaints.
reasoning: A consistent resolution process limits ongoing customer impact and reveals whether corrective actions are effective.

title: Contain Critical Product Quality Risks
description: Take urgent, evidence-led action when credible reports indicate a severe defect, safety concern, or widespread product failure.
actions: Immediately assess the specific product, batch, and severity of reports.
Stop sale or dispatch of affected items when warranted by safety or material-defect evidence.
Escalate to responsible leadership, suppliers, and relevant authorities where legally required.
reasoning: Potentially severe product failures require rapid containment and formal escalation, based on verified evidence.

title: Initiate an Urgent Product Safety Assessment
description: Arrange an urgent technical assessment when feedback suggests a possible safety-related product issue.
actions: Preserve complaints, photos, returned items, and batch records.
Have a qualified person assess the potential hazard.
Follow applicable reporting, recall, and customer-notification obligations.
reasoning: Safety signals should be assessed by qualified personnel rather than treated as ordinary product dissatisfaction.

title: Isolate Confirmed High-Impact Defective Stock
description: Limit further exposure to stock confirmed to have a severe or widespread defect while a resolution is arranged.
actions: Trace affected stock and orders.
Segregate confirmed affected inventory.
Coordinate replacement, refund, repair, or recall steps as appropriate.
reasoning: Isolation is justified when the affected stock has been identified and the potential customer impact is substantial.

title: Coordinate a Critical Quality Response
description: Create a single accountable response to a serious quality incident and keep customers informed of verified next steps.
actions: Assign an incident owner and decision-makers.
Set a response timeline and record all decisions.
Issue accurate customer updates and avoid unsupported claims.
reasoning: A coordinated response reduces confusion and supports timely, consistent action.

title: Verify Recovery Before Resuming Normal Sales
description: Confirm that corrective measures have worked before returning affected products to normal handling or sale.
actions: Require documented inspection or testing of corrective changes.
Check a representative sample of corrected stock.
Record approval to resume and monitor subsequent feedback closely.
reasoning: Resuming only after verification helps prevent a critical issue from recurring.
